modSecLevels.0: EMERGENCY - is generated from correlation of anomaly scoring data where there is an inbound attack and an outbound leakage
modSecLevels.1: ALERT - is generated from correlation where there is an inbound attack and an outbound application level error
modSecLevels.2: CRITICAL - Anomaly Score of 5. Is the highest severity level possible without correlation. It is normally generated by the web attack rules (40 level files)
modSecLevels.3: ERROR - Anomaly Score of 4. Is generated mostly from outbound leakage rules (50 level files)
modSecLevels.4: WARNING - Anomaly Score of 3. Is generated by malicious client rules (35 level files)
modSecLevels.5: NOTICE - Anomaly Score of 2. Is generated by the Protocol policy and anomaly files

active_response.description:
Active Response is an OSSEC-driven (IDS) feature of Imunify360 which has been re-engineered to make it capable of blocking access to a specific server port being attacked. 
The purpose of the feature is significantly reducing false positive rate while increasing its capabilities to detect and block aggressive brute force requests.
active_response.label: Active response

catch_lfd_events.description: Lets Imunify360 manage CSF events and IP lists
catch_lfd_events.label: Manage CSF Events and Lists

enable.label: Enable WebShield
enable.description: When the option is off, WebShield and GreyList are disabled. A disabled state is recommended for the servers with a small amount of RAM. A disabled option along with enabled "Minimized WAF Ruleset" will switch Imunify360 to the "Low Resource Usage" mode.

known_proxies_support.description: Allows to recognize and block IPs with suspicious activity behind CloudFlare and MaxCDN
known_proxies_support.label: Detect IPs behind CDN

splash_screen.description: Show JavaScript challenge page to the visitors with suspicious IPs in order to verify whether they are bots or humans. Will drastically reduce server load and will not affect legitimate bots e.g. search bots, CDN providers and similar.
splash_screen.note: This feature will require an additional 20MB of RAM.
splash_screen.label: Anti-bot protection

panel_protection.label: cPanel account protection
panel_protection.description:
Show JavaScript challenge to any user trying to access hosting panel interface. It will prevent bots from compromising and using the account.
 Note: legitimate automation services that access web UI/API must be whitelisted manually.

compromisedUserPasswordReset.label: Compromised accounts password reset
compromisedUserPasswordReset.description: The owners of accounts that were flagged as compromised will be forced to reset their passwords during the next login.

compromisedUserAdminNotification.label: Enable email notifications about compromised accounts
compromisedUserAdminNotification.description: The admin of hosts where users with compromised passwords were found will receive email notifications with a list of the corresponding users.

enable.label: PAM brute-force attack protection
enable.description: This feature enables an advanced brute-force protection technique based on the combination of PAM module authorization, RBL check and IP blacklisting.

eximDovecotProtection.label: Exim+Dovecot brute-force attack protection
eximDovecotProtection.description: This feature enables advanced protection against Dovecot brute-force attacks.

ftpProtection.label: FTP brute-force attack protection
ftpProtection.description: This feature enables advanced protection against FTP brute-force attacks.

appSpecificRuleset.label: Apply CMS-specific WAF Rules
appSpecificRuleset.description:
Domain rules are applied based on detected content management systems (WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, etc)
and their plugins. It allows making WAF rules more effective to protect websites and reduce the number of false positives.
All changes (new or removed domains, new or removed content management systems) are applied within a day.
When disabled, the default Imunify360 WAF rules are applied to all domains.

ruleSet.label: Minimized ModSec Ruleset
ruleSet.description: When this option is on, Imunify WAF rules with a high memory footprint are disabled, but critical ruleset is enabled. It will significantly reduce memory usage. Recommended for the servers with a small amount of RAM. An enabled option along with disabled WebShield will switch Imunify360 to the "Low Resource Usage" mode.

wordPressAccountCompromise.label: WordPress Account Compromise Prevention
wordPressAccountCompromise.description: This option enables a security setting for WordPress websites when users use weak account passwords listed in brute-force vocabulary. It takes a user that is trying to log in to WordPress onto a special page with an alert message and forces to reset a password to prevent unauthorized account use.
wordPressAccountCompromise.warning: This switch disables “Weak password login prevention” and allows to use weak passwords, but it does not disable heuristics level protection for the compromised accounts.

cleanup.description: Truncate a file instead of removal, making it zero-length.

stopProcessOnCleanup.label: Stop processes running a malware file
stopProcessOnCleanup.description: During malware cleanup, stop processes of the file owner that run the detected file or hold it open, so they cannot restore it. Web servers, workers shared by several accounts, root and system processes are never stopped.
stopProcessOnCleanup.modes: Report only: nothing is stopped; each process that would be stopped is listed in the malware history and the agent log. Default: Imunify manages this setting and may turn it on step by step.

warning.remoteip_loopback_untrusted: Apache may not trust 127.0.0.1 as a proxy; if so, visitors proxied by WebShield are seen as 127.0.0.1 and their WAF incidents are lost. The cause is in /var/log/imunify360/console.log and in the output of imunify360-agent doctor. Usually i360.remoteip.conf is missing: reinstall the Imunify360 firewall package for your panel (imunify360-firewall-cpanel, -plesk, -directadmin) to restore it (on Ubuntu/Debian add -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confmiss)
warning.waf_incidents_attributed_to_loopback: WAF incidents are attributed to 127.0.0.1 although the requests came through a local proxy such as WebShield, so the real visitors are lost and these incidents are dropped. Make the web server take the client address from X-Forwarded-For sent from 127.0.0.1 (Apache: mod_remoteip with RemoteIPInternalProxy 127.0.0.1 and RemoteIPHeader X-Forwarded-For; LiteSpeed: 'Use Client IP in Header' set to 'Trusted IP Only' and 127.0.0.1T in the Access Control allowed list)
warning.scan_intensity_io_cfq: This option is effective with CFQ IO scheduler only
warning.scan_hyperscan_no_ssse3: Requires SSSE3 CPU instruction set. If you are using QEMU/KVM, make sure you don't use the default or severely outdated CPU model.

rules.R1: the file itself was the running program
rules.R2: an allowed interpreter (shell, PHP, Python or Perl) held the file open
rules.R3: the file was the script named on its command line (PHP 8.0 or earlier, Python, Perl)
rules.R4: a PHP worker of the account held the file open

reasons.no_rule: Imunify does not stop this kind of program (it only read the file)
reasons.deny_list: the program is never stopped (web server, system service or shared worker)
reasons.uid: the process runs as another user
reasons.not_hosting_account: the file owner is not a hosting account
reasons.write_only_handle: the process only writes to the file
reasons.read_failed: the process could not be inspected
reasons.no_pidfd: the server's kernel cannot stop a process safely
reasons.could_not_freeze: the process could not be paused before the cleanup
reasons.freeze_timeout: the cleanup took too long, so the paused process was resumed
reasons.released_after_restart: the agent restarted while the process was paused, so it was resumed
reasons.respawning: the process keeps restarting, so stopping is paused for this file
reasons.no_longer_matches: the process no longer runs the file
reasons.stop_cap: too many processes to stop in one cleanup

limits.rule: stopping is not enabled for this kind of match on this server
limits.gone: the file was already deleted, and stopping is not enabled for that case on this server
limits.title: the process was linked to the file only by its cut-off process title
limits.relative: the process was linked to the file only by a relative script name, which may point to another file
limits.stop_cap: too many processes to stop in one cleanup

proactive.title: Proactive Defense
proactive.text:
Imunify360's Proactive Defense protects websites against zero-day attacks - it stops even the malware that no scanner is able to detect. It identifies attacks on your Linux web servers in real time, then blocks potentially malicious executions automatically and with zero latency. 

 Proactive Defense uses a unique method of identifying security risks - it analyzes what scripts do rather than what is actually in the code.

reputation.title: Website Reputation Monitoring
reputation.text: We analyze if your site or IPs are blocked by any blacklists and notify you if they are. Your site reputation is very important. For example, if you are added to the Google blacklist as a site that distributes malware, you will be excluded from Google search results, which can be devastating for business. If you get on an RBL list as a spammer, your emails to customers might not be delivered. If you don't proactively monitor your website’s reputation, you might not find out about blacklisting for weeks or even months, at which point the problem could become ruinous.

malware.title: Malware Scanner
malware.text:
Detect any type of malicious file, including backdoors, web-shells, viruses, hacker tools, ‘blackhat SEO’ scripts, phishing pages, and many others. 

 If malware is detected, automatically remove it with one click. Advanced file deobfuscation techniques enable detection of encrypted malicious code embedded in files, over 97% of which can be cleaned automatically.

firewall.title: Advanced Firewall
firewall.text:
Imunify360 offers advanced firewall protection that uses herd immunity and artificial intelligence to detect new threats and protect all servers that run the software. The firewall is capable of defending against brute force attacks, DoS attacks, and port scans. 

 The firewall tightly integrates with mod_security web application firewalls to dramatically enhance its usefulness. In combination with WAF, we can stop the majority of web application attacks even before they start. An advanced SplashScreen system is employed to reduce false positives and make sure that valid customers can reach your website.

patch.title: Patch Management
patch.text1: Rebootless Secure Kernel powered by KernelCare is a component that keeps your server secure by automatically patching kernels without having to reboot the server. Its agent checks for new patches every four hours and automatically applies them to the running server without any performance impact. KernelCare keeps your kernel updated to help you avoid disastrous incidents.
patch.text2: Hardened PHP is a component that ensures your web server security by patching all PHP versions against known vulnerabilities, allowing you to run any version of PHP without having to update programs to accommodate newer versions.
